*[Bug 19104] New: Fix buffer overread in R_is_redirection_tty*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19104>

            Bug ID: 19104
           Summary: Fix buffer overread in R_is_redirection_tty
           Product: R
           Version: R-devel (trunk)
          Hardware: Other
                OS: Other
            Status: UNCONFIRMED
          Severity: normal
          Priority: P5
         Component: Low-level
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:h.wickham@gmail.com|h.wickham@gmail.com>

`R_is_redirection_tty` has a buffer overrun. A comment in its source code
identifies "note that fnInfo->FileName is not null terminated", but doesn't do
anything about it, which causes the occasional failure for parallel testthat on
Windows (<https://github.com/r-lib/testthat/issues/2284>).

This looks like a simple fix:
<https://patch-diff.githubusercontent.com/raw/r-devel/r-svn/pull/275.patch>. (You
may want to drop the very defensive validation of `fnInfo->FileNameLength`, but
I included for completeness.)

*[Bug 19105] New: Provide a traceback when crashing on Windows*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19105>

            Bug ID: 19105
           Summary: Provide a traceback when crashing on Windows
           Product: R
           Version: R 4.6.x
          Hardware: All
                OS: Windows 64-bit
            Status: NEW
          Severity: normal
          Priority: P5
         Component: Wishlist
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:ikrylov@disroot.org|ikrylov@disroot.org>

Created attachment 3760
  --> <https://bugs.r-project.org/attachment.cgi?id=3760&action=edit>
Use VEH to print a traceback when crashing on Windows

Currently, when a package crashes on Win-Builder during tests or examples, the
output just stops. It takes effort to determine that there was, in fact, a
crash (and not timeout / storage becoming full / hardware issues / gremlins),
and there's not always enough information to determine where the crash
occurred. Sometimes we're lucky and the crash [is easily
reproducible](<https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-package-devel/2026q2/012376.html>).
[Other
times](<https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-package-devel/2023q4/010170.html>) the
crash [remains
elusive](<https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-package-devel/2026q3/012434.html>) and
we're stumped until we can obtain more information (with luck, the same crash
shows up with sanitizers on Linux).

Conversely, on most Unix-like systems (with working `sigaction()` and
`sigaltstack()`), the signal handler makes the crash evident and (if the heap
is sufficiently intact) provides an R-level traceback. On Windows, R could use
[vectored exception
handling](<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/debug/vectored-exception-handling>)
to catch a fatal exception in a similar manner. 

The attached patch takes the common, R-specific parts of `sigactionSegv` and
`win32_segv`
([unused](<https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-devel/2024-June/083524.html>)) and
makes R call them from the respective system-specific handlers. Currently it's
wired up to minimise changes in `src/main/main.c` and to leave Windows-specific
code under `src/gnuwin32`, although the result feels awkward. Perhaps it's
better to make `fatal_traceback()` declared in `Defn.h`, `attribute_hidden`, to
be called from handlers registered in `src/main/main.c` or
`src/gnuwin32/system.c`?

```
$ ../../bin/x64/Rscript.exe -e '.Fortran(stats:::C_lowesw, numeric(), 100L,
numeric(), integer())'

 *** caught access violation at address 0x00007ffb33252192 ***
accessing address 0xffffffffffffffff, action: read

Traceback:
 1: .Fortran(stats:::C_lowesw, numeric(), 100L, numeric(), integer())
An irrecoverable exception occurred. R is aborting now ...
```
